camps.name: Perfection Lake and Inspiration Lake basin camps
camps.why: Roomier, well-used benches beside the two lakes with water close; the scramble to Prusik Pass and the face adds under an hour each way versus Gnome Tarn.

camps.name: Gnome Tarn
camps.why: The closest camp to the south face, about 15 minutes away, so both nights are here with no repacking and summit day starts fresh.

camps.name: Colchuck Lake designated campsites
camps.why: Sleeping here moves the Aasgard Pass grind off day one, but it leaves a long haul to the south face; a Colchuck zone permit does not cover the Core.

plan_conflict: Camp notes on file list the Perfection/Inspiration basin camps as main, but the plan and trip reports have parties sleeping both nights at Gnome Tarn.

new_camps.name: Gnome Tarn
new_camps.why: The closest camp to the south face, about 15 minutes away, so both nights are here with no repacking and summit day starts fresh.
new_camps.permit: Overnight permit required May 15 to Oct 31; a Core Enchantments permit covers this area.
new_camps.notes: A small tarn about 15 minutes from the south face of Prusik, reached by leaving the Perfection Lake route toward Prusik Pass. Camp only on already-impacted sites; no fires above 5,000 ft.

camps.name: Inspiration and Perfection Lakes
camps.why: The most-used benches between the two lakes, with water at hand; the signed path to Prusik Pass starts nearby, adding under an hour each way versus Gnome Tarn.

camps.name: Tarn below Isolation Lake
camps.why: Easy water, fewer insects and shelter below the open benches, but about two miles and some climbing from the peak; a quieter base for a longer stay.

plan_conflict: Camp notes on file list Inspiration and Perfection Lakes as main, but the plan and trip reports have parties sleeping at Gnome Tarn, which is not on file for this route.

camps.name: Sherpa south basin camp
camps.why: Lower camp at 6,200 ft above the Ingalls Creek trail: a shorter day one, but a longer, higher summit day than sleeping at Table Rock.

camps.name: Table Rock bivy, upper Sherpa basin
camps.why: The flat block at about 7,400 ft is where most parties sleep: it cuts the summit day to a short walk to the ridge, with snow-remnant water close by in early season.

camps.name: Beverly and De Roux campgrounds and the North Fork Teanaway roadside camps
camps.why: Car camps for the night before the walk-in; a late arrival can sleep here, but the 2-day plan itself spends its only night at the basin bivy.

camps.name: Ingalls Creek valley camps below the Sherpa and Argonaut south sides
camps.why: Creek-side camps near the trail with reliable water; used by parties who stretch the trip to three days or stop short of the basin with heavy packs.

plan_conflict: Camp notes on file list both the south basin camp and Table Rock as main; reports put the usual night at the Table Rock bivy near 7,400 ft (the plan says treeline, about 7,000 ft).

camps.name: Upper Mountaineer Creek bench
camps.why: Flat camp near 5,400 ft with creek water for filtering, the usual base on the north side; a higher bivy near the crest saves effort but has no reliable water.

plan_conflict: The plan puts night 1 on a ledge near 7,800 ft below the crest, but the camps parties actually report on the north side are the Mountaineer Creek bench (about 5,400 ft) and the flat area near 5,800 ft.

camps.name: Core Enchantments / Prusik Pass area
camps.why: The Core camp area works if you are linking Prusik or High Priest, but it adds a long cross-basin walk and a separate Core permit for a Temple-only trip.

camps.name: Upper Snow Lake
camps.why: A halfway stop on the Snow Lakes trail that splits the long, hot climb, but leaves a still-steep day to Tamarack Meadows with a pack.

new_camps.name: Tamarack Meadows
new_camps.why: The benches above Temple Canyon put the climb a short walk away, so both nights are here and summit day starts from camp.
new_camps.permit: Overnight permit required May 15 to Oct 31.
new_camps.notes: Reached by the Snow Lakes trail past Nada Lake, then a faint climber's path up Temple Canyon that fades near the top. Camp only on existing sites.

plan_conflict: Camp notes on file list Upper Snow Lake and the Core area as main, but the plan walks to Tamarack Meadows on day 1 and returns there the second night.

new_camps.name: Viviane Campsite (Lake Viviane)
new_camps.why: The one established camp at the lake, with water and the climb close by, so all three nights are spent here after the long haul in.
new_camps.water: Lake Viviane and its outlet stream.
new_camps.permit: Overnight permit required May 15 to Oct 31; sources disagree on whether the lake is inside the Core zone.
new_camps.notes: Several sites with views over Upper Snow Lake and the valley; goats visit camp. Camp only on existing sites; no fires above 5,000 ft.

camps.name: Dolomite Tower bivy caves
camps.why: Three flat platforms in shallow caves right of the start, one person each, so the 14 pitches begin from the base; spray blows in during wind and rain.

plan_conflict: Recent parties often do the approach, climb and descent car-to-car in one long day (about 12.5 hours), using the caves only when slower or splitting the trip.
